primary_origins.text: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)

FGDC-1423.title: 2002 (Jan. - Feb.) U.S. Bottom Trawl Survey Leg 2 Data for Arrowtooth Flounder on the Outter Continental Shelf and Upper Slope of the Gulf of Alaska West of Kodiak Island - R/V Miller Freeman (Cruise ID: MF2002-01)
FGDC-1423.abstract_xml:
The Alaska Fisheries Science Center FOCI program conducted a bottom trawl survey on the outer continental shelf and upper slope of the Gulf of Alaska west of Kodiak Island.

Bottom trawls were conducted to collect juvenile walleye pollock for otoliths and adult arrowtooth flounder for sexual maturity and spawning studies. Arrowtooth flounder data include lengths, otoliths, maturities, and gonads. Data (CTD) on physical characteristics of water in the area were also collected.

Other collected samples include Cholorophyll, nutrient, microzooplankton, sebastes, bathymasterid larvae, capelin rough count, and quantitative tows preserved in formalin. Zooplankton data and data on physical characteristics of the water column were also be collected.

Cruise ID: MF2002-01 (29 Jan. - 9 Feb. 2002)
Survey vessels: R/V Miller Freeman

For preliminary survey results see http://www.afsc.noaa.gov/race/surveys/cruise_archives/cruises2002/results_MF2002-01.pdf

FGDC-1930.abstract_xml:
<abstract>This scientific report summarizes the results of workshops organized by the PICES-GLOBEC Climate Change and Carrying Capacity Program held just prior to the Eighth Annual Meeting in Vladivostok, Russia, in October 1999. In addition, a very successful modelling workshop was subsequently convened in Nemuro, Japan, the following January.  

The MONITOR Task Team meeting was much devoted to an extensive review and discussion of international efforts in GOOS (Global Ocean Observing System), which will serve as a framework for questions about how to get oceanographic data into a useable form in a timely manner. The data from these new initiatives will form the basis for the monitoring systems of the future.  

The REX Task Team held a workshop to review the population dynamics of herring and euphausiids around the Pacific Rim. Typical of small pelagic animals, large changes in the abundance of these key members of coastal ecosystems are observed over time, and interesting data on the changes in feeding success and overwinter energy depletion were reported. An interesting development within the North Pacific are the reports on longer-term fluctuations in herring abundance, which will no doubt serve to provide a better perspective on the short-term fluctuations evident when only data from modern fisheries is examined. A number of interesting relationships were also noted between the abundance of herring and euphausiids from around the Pacific Rim.

the MODEL Task Team met to discuss developments during the past year and to make the final plans for an intensive workshop scheduled for Nemuro, Japan, in January 2000. The extensive report from that meeting is included here, and describes the results of a substantial effort by many members of the PICES modelling community to develop a consensus on the essential elements of an ecosystem model for the North Pacific Ocean; their progress in doing so will provide an essential stepping stone towards a better understanding of what aspects of the ecosystem are most important to measure and monitor in the future.

<abstract>The BASS Workshop on "The development of a conceptual model of the Subarctic Pacific basin exosystem" discusses the possibility of applying ECOPATH/ECOSIM to the modeling of subarctic gyre ecosystems, based on presentations, the extended abstracts of which appear in the report. The MODEL Workshop on "Strategies for coupling higher and lower trophic level marine ecosystem models" discussed the strategic considerations necessary in coupling higher and lower trophic level marine ecosystem models and the extension and improvement of the prototype lower trophic level PICES NEMURO Model. The workshop report contains abstracts, extended abstracts, and fully prepared reports presented at the workshop.  

The MONITOR Workshop on "Progress in monitoring the North Pacific" reviewed ongoing and/or planned monitoring programs in North Pacific and made a number of pertinent recommendations. The summary of the workshop is followed by extended abstracts of papers given at the meeting.  

The REX Workshop on "Trends in herring populations and trophodynamics" summarized generalizations, observations and hypotheses on herring populations and identified the need to add F (fish) into the current crop of NPZ (Nutrients - Phytoplankton - Zooplankton) models that are available.

Publication Title: Morskoi Atlas = Marine atlas. Text in Russian. For full detailed English translation see 'An Evaluation of the "Morskoi Atlas" (With Translations from Volumes I and II)'.

The Morskoi Atlas is devided into three parts: Volume I, navigation and geography; Volume II, physical geography; Volume III, military and political geography.

Contains a comprehensive treatment of the marine environment of the earth. Contains sea charts and maps of important ports and naval bases, bathymetry, sea level, nature and velocity of currents, ice boundaries, ocean routes, national frontiers, earthquakes, volcanos, sediments, sea surface temperature, salinity, and density, range of tides, wind waves and swell, distribution of cetacea, sirenia, pinnipeds, ocean fishes, marine birds and algae, atmospheric pressure, cloudiness, fog, and storms.

FGDC-2587.abstract_xml:
Publication Title: "Sammlung Gemein Verstandlicher Wisseuschaftlicher Vortrage" (Collection of Scientific Lectures). Volume XIII No. 289-312, pages 821-884.

Lecture title: "Die Tiefsee und Ihre Boden- und Temperatur- Verhaltnisse" ("The Deep-Sea and Its Ground and Temperature Conditions"). Author: Boguslawski, G. Von. Text in German.

Information in this collection dates back to the 18th century for daily, monthly, seasonal, and annual tabular summaries, and the 19th century for weather maps. In these summaries, definitions are:
1. Hourly/daily/monthly/seasonal/annual data -- values determined for each consecutive period, e.g. monthly temperature data: Jan 1900, Feb 1900, etc.
2. Long-term data -- values determined over a period of years, e.g. long-term monthly temperature data using Jan 1901, Jan 1902, etc.

This book contains tables of hourly sea surface and subsurface temperature recorded at 3 ships during voyages round the world in Pacific, Atlantic, and Indian Oceans, from 1873 through 1876. Also contains conditions of the sea floor ocean circulation and temperature distribution. Graphs contain the following data: - hourly sea surface and subsurface temperature Maps contain the following data: - depths of Pacific, Atlantic, and Indian Oceans.

FGDC-3815.title: The Results of Trawling Survey in the Epipelagic Layer of the Russian Economic Zone in the Bering Sea During, August - October, 2002
FGDC-3815.abstract_xml:
The results of complex survey in the epipelagic layer of the western Bering Sea in September - October, 2002 on the research vessel TINRO are examined. The data on oceanologic conditions is presented along with information on allocation and abundance on main zooplankton groups, and quantitative distribution of nekton. The abundance and biomass of fish and cephalopods in the western Bering Sea and adjacent Pacific waters are evaluated. The quantitative distribution of salmon is studied very closely. The information on salmon feeding in different areas of the western Bering Sea is included. The brief analysis of the current status of plankton and nekton epipelagic communities of the western Bering Sea is offered.

[Reference: Temnykh, O.S., A.N. Starovoytov, I.I. Glebov, G.V. Khen, A.Ya. Efimkin, A.M. Slabinsky, V.V. Sviridov. 2003. FGDC-3850.title: Benthic Habitats of Willapa Bay, Washington, 1995
FGDC-3850.abstract_xml:
In June 1995, the Columbia River Estuary Study Taskforce (CREST) acquired 295 true color aerial photographs (1:12,000) of Willapa Bay, Washington, from the State of Washington Department of Transportation (WDOT), suitable for the interpretation of submerged rooted aquatic vascular plant populations. In August 1995, field surveys were conducted by a team composed of staff from Oregon State University, CREST, and the Washington Department of Natural Resources, for spectral signature development and verification as well as habitat observation. The submerged plant populations were interpreted and mapped from the photographs and transferred onto State of Washington 1:12,000 Orthophoto maps (USGS 7.5' quadrangle). The interpretations were digitized into a geographic information system (GIS) for the creation of a habitat polygon map. All interpretation, digitization and photography acquisition were according to stringent parameters detailed in the Coastal Change Analysis Program (C-CAP) Protocol (NMFS Technical Document 123). Two datasets were used as ancillary information to complement the interpreted habitat polygons. In 1996, color aerial videography was obtained from WDOT for post mapping verification and accuracy assessments. Marine Resources Consultants, Inc. and the University of Washington collected videography from 29 underwater transects to verify the deep-water edge of selected seagrass beds in the southern portion of the bay. The date, time, geographic coordinates and depth were updated every 2 to 4 seconds and recorded directly on the videotape images. Latitude and longitude were provided by a differentially corrected global positioning system (GPS). The initial presence/absence map of SAV produced by CREST was later segmented by depth to discriminate between two very different seagrass communities and support field accuracy assessment. Final field verification of the data by personnel from CREST and the NOAA Coastal Services Center was conducted in the Summer of 1997.

The benthic data is classified according to the System for Classification of Habitats in Estuarine and Marine Environments (SCHEME). This system is fully described in "Development of a System for Classification of Habitats in Estuarine and Marine Environments (SCHEME) for Florida, Report to U.S. EPA - Gulf of Mexico Program, Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, Florida Marine Research Institute. Review Draft 12/04/02."

This data is meant only for use as it pertains to the CD-ROM Product. Custom_Order_Process: Contact NOAA Coastal Services Center's Clearinghouse Manager and request a copy of "Benthic Habitats of Willa Bay, Florida, 1995, CD-ROM". Alternatively, fill out a CSC Product Request Form at .http://www.csc.noaa.gov/clearinghouse/prodreq_form.html. The data set can also be downloaded in a zip format at http://www.csc.noaa.gov/benthic/data/northwest/willapa.htm.

FGDC-4181.abstract_xml: <abstract>Data from merchant ships travelling between British Columbia and Japan, from 1980-1990 (Canada Ace), 1995 to 2000, continuing (Skaugran), and 1999-2000, continuing (Alligator Hope). Data collected include surface total carbon dioxide, alkalinity, nutrients, chlorophyll a, carbon-13 in seawater, and atmospheric carbon-13. Underway measurements include position, time, temperature and salinity. Skaugran samples and data were collected 3-4 times daily by scientific staff and once daily by ship`s engineers until 1999, then were reduced to daily engineer`s samples. Alligator Hope samples were collected 3 times daily.</abstract>
